name: Renato Mancuso
title: Associate Professor; Director, Cyber-Physical Systems Lab
department: Computer Science; affiliated Electrical and Computer Engineering
fitReason: Strong applied robot-learning and deployment fit: neural flight control, online RL adaptation and embedded reliability, alongside a broader real-time computer-systems agenda.

physicalEvidence.summary: Sim-Anchored Learning v3 (May 1, 2025) reports a real racing quadrotor with MATEK-F722 flight controller. A ground station fine-tunes anchored RL policies from flight data and transmits replacements while onboard inference continues; experiments include tethered failure tests and unconstrained flights. Physical evidence concerns low-level attitude response, not autonomous mission planning. First author Bassel El Mabsout and coauthor Shahin Roozkhosh are independently listed as Mancuso-supervised PhD alumni, and the current lab explicitly identifies neural flight control as a research area. The 2026 Lyapunov/FPL paper uses simulation and is not additional hardware evidence.

shortVisit.summary: Current central CS profile invites master and PhD research inquiries but does not explicitly invite outside-university short visitors. CV records 2022–24 visiting PhD scholars for three to seven months; this is historical precedent rather than an eight-week external-master offer.

scoreReasons.fit: Substantive RL, neural flight control and sim-to-real methodology; some lab activity is systems architecture rather than robot learning.
scoreReasons.physical: Actual flight adaptation and current lab-topic plus independently verified directed-student lineage, not mere coauthorship.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: General master/PhD inquiry and past doctoral visitors do not establish an external short-master invitation.
scoreReasons.freshness: 2026 neural-control publication and September 2026 active lab news, with May 2025 primary hardware revision.

name: Hyunglae Lee
title: Associate Professor; Director, Neuromuscular Control and Human Robotics Laboratory
department: School for Engineering of Matter, Transport and Energy; Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
fitReason: Substantive learned adaptation of real human-interactive robots through DQN gait personalization, GP/Bayesian impedance tuning and learned state-driven soft assistance.

physicalEvidence.summary: March 2026 primary soft back-support paper executes subject-specific random-forest state and load classification on Raspberry Pi 5; outputs select pneumatic pressure and clutch engagement during actual on-body lifting/lowering. It is closed-loop learned mode selection, not an end-to-end neural torque policy. April 2026 ASU reporting independently confirms lead student Rohan Khatavkar is co-supervised by Lee and Sun. Separate 2025 work uses DQN-guided in-situ gait-perturbation selection and GP/Bayesian optimization on an actual wearable ankle robot. Healthy-participant demonstrations do not establish clinical efficacy.

shortVisit.summary: Lab Opportunities page recruits MS/PhD students and local FURI/Honors undergraduates. It requests a CV and cover letter but does not explicitly specify external nondegree master visitors or eight-week research placements.

scoreReasons.fit: Learned human-in-the-loop control and personalization are central to verified current robot work.
scoreReasons.physical: Actual wearable actuation and human experiments with current co-supervised lead-student linkage.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Degree-focused recruitment is not an explicit external short-visit invitation.
scoreReasons.freshness: March 2026 primary learned-actuation paper, April 2026 official project attribution and current ASU appointment.

name: Marcos Quiñones-Grueiro
title: Research Scientist; Adjunct Professor of Computer Science
department: Institute for Software Integrated Systems; Computer Science
fitReason: Direct robotics relevance through actual hybrid PPO/LSTM aerial control and current safe continual RL. Highway speed-limit control is separate broader physical-CPS evidence.

physicalEvidence.summary: DX2024 primary paper reports five actual octocopter flights at Fort Devens with MIT Lincoln Laboratory assistance. A simulation-trained PPO agent runs on a ground station every 0.5 s, adjusting horizontal reference velocities based on an LSTM disturbance estimator; ArduPilot handles lower-level flight control. The paper calls the real platform DJI S100 and distinguishes the simulated Tarot T-18. This is actual learned supervisory control, not just recorded UAV data. Physical 20 reflects older off-site collaborative deployment with no verified current Vanderbilt visitor access. Separate2025 highway VSL work controls physical signs, not robot vehicles; April 2026 safe-continual-RL robot benchmarks are simulation.

shortVisit.summary: Current homepage records an August 2026 one-month graduate return visit and March 2026 three-month graduate visit, plus an August 2025 three-month foreign graduate visit. These demonstrate graduate visiting precedent but are not an open invitation, verified master classification, or 2027 availability.
